title: implement forward_and_back

atoms.evidence: Solution hand-writes the forward graph (d=a*b, e=log(c), f=d*e, g=log(f)) then manually plumbs grad_out through log_back/multiply_back0/back1 calls without autograd — the warm-up scaffold this exercise is named after
dg_df = log_back(grad_out=final_grad_out, out=g, x=f); dg_dc = log_back(dg_de, e, c) — log-back called twice in the chain
dg_dd = multiply_back0(dg_df, f, d, e); dg_de = multiply_back1(dg_df, f, d, e); dg_da = multiply_back0(dg_dd, d, a, b); dg_db = multiply_back1(dg_dd, d, a, b) — 4 multiply_back calls
Solution dispatches to multiply_back0 for arg-0 (x) and multiply_back1 for arg-1 (y) per each multiply node
final_grad_out = np.ones_like(g) — markdown explicitly explains 'we'll just be using the default behaviour where v is a tensor of 1s — equivalent to L = g.sum()' (directional derivative)
Every _back call uses the (grad_out, out, x[, y]) signature; the exercise drills the convention by repetition across 6 calls

notes: 6 atoms — matches seed prediction of 7 (1 less). The 'see backprop by hand' exercise — pure plumbing of the per-op _back functions without any autograd framework. Predecessor of the §6 backprop traversal.
